saints.name: St. Dominic Savio
saints.title: Youth
saints.shortBlurb: A boy of the Oratory under St. John Bosco who resolved to “die rather than sin,” dead before his fifteenth year…
biography: Born on 2 April 1842 at Riva near Turin, the son of a blacksmith and a seamstress, Dominic Savio made his first Communion at seven and at twelve met John Bosco, who received him into the Oratory at Valdocco. The boy resolved at once upon holiness, taking for his motto, 'Death rather than sin'.

At the Oratory he served Mass daily and in 1856 gathered companions into the Sodality of the Immaculate Conception. When two boys who had stuffed the school stove with rubbish threw the blame on him, he bore the punishment in silence rather than accuse them; he is therefore invoked as patron of the falsely accused.

His health, never strong, gave way; sent home to Mondonio and weakened by the bleedings then in fashion, he died on 9 March 1857, not yet fifteen, saying he saw something wonderful. John Bosco wrote his life; Pius X advanced his cause; Pius XII beatified him in 1950 and canonized him in 1954, and the Church has named him patron of young people and of choirboys.
saints.knownFor: Youthful holiness formed under St. John Bosco.
